businessRules.rule: A staff record is held in two parts: the general record, and the salary section — the agreed salary, the pay basis and every salary generated for that employee. They are separate so one can be hidden without hiding the other.
The Principal and the Super Admin see the whole record. The Principal and Accounts see the salary section for every employee.
The School Admin sees and maintains the general record, but the salary section is hidden from them — on the record itself and on every list, report and export.
No other role sees any employee's salary. An employee sees their own record and their own salary only.

The rule is applied wherever a salary can appear — the staff record, a payroll run, a list, a report or an export — not only on the record screen. A salary leaked through an export is leaked as surely as one shown on a screen.
The Super Admin can change which roles hold each of these rights, in the same way as the approval configuration. The rights are not written into the software.
A change to the configuration is recorded with who made it and when. It decides who sees what people are paid, and a change nobody can trace is a change nobody can question.
Hiding is not filtering after the fact. A role without the right never receives the salary figure, rather than receiving it and having it hidden in the interface.
An employee's own salary is always visible to them, whatever the configuration says. A person is entitled to know what they are paid.
Where a report or an export would contain a salary the requester may not see, the column is omitted rather than the whole report being refused. The rest of the report is still useful.
The configuration is read at the moment of each request, so a change takes effect at once rather than at the next sign-in.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens the configuration and sees which roles hold each right.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows the four rights and the roles currently holding each.

basicFlow.userAction: Changes which roles hold a right.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Applies the change at once and records who made it and when.
Returns the whole record, general and salary alike.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens and maintains the same record.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Returns the general record without the salary section, which is not sent at all rather than hidden in the interface.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens the salary section for payroll.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Returns the agreed salary, the pay basis and the generated salaries for every employee.
Applies the same rule to the payroll run, every list, every report and every export, omitting a salary column the requester may not see.
Returns their own record and their own salary, and no other employee's.

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin runs a staff list or an export
alternateFlows.behaviour: The salary column is omitted from the output rather than the export being refused, so the rest stays useful (BR-3, BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: A payroll run is opened by a role without the right
alternateFlows.behaviour: The salary figures are not returned. A payroll run shows salaries and is covered by the same rule (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: The Super Admin grants the right to a further role
alternateFlows.behaviour: The change takes effect at once, since the configuration is read at each request rather than at sign-in (BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: An employee opens their own salary
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is visible to them whatever the configuration says, since a person is entitled to know what they are paid (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin needs the salary to do their work
alternateFlows.behaviour: The right is granted deliberately through the configuration rather than worked around. This is the point the contradiction with salary setting has to be resolved at.

exceptions.condition: The School Admin requests the salary section directly by its address
exceptions.systemResponse: It is not returned. The rule is enforced on the server, not in the interface (BR-8).
exceptions.messageShown: You do not have permission to view this record.

exceptions.condition: A role is removed from every right that permits payroll to run
exceptions.systemResponse: The change is refused, since payroll would then be impossible.
exceptions.messageShown: Accounts must retain sight of salary, or payroll cannot be run.

exceptions.condition: A report is built that would contain a salary the requester may not see
exceptions.systemResponse: The column is omitted and the report is still produced (BR-10).
exceptions.messageShown: The salary column has been omitted from this report.

exceptions.condition: A non-Super Admin attempts to change the configuration
exceptions.messageShown: Only the Super Admin can change visibility rights.

exceptions.condition: An employee attempts to see another employee's salary
exceptions.messageShown: You do not have permission to view this record.

exceptions.condition: The Super Admin removes their own right to see the record
exceptions.systemResponse: It is refused, since nobody could then restore the configuration.
exceptions.messageShown: The Super Admin cannot remove their own access to this configuration.

departures.requirement: A role without the right never receives the salary figure in any response. Hiding it in the interface is not sufficient, because the response can be read directly.
The rule is enforced on the record, the payroll run, every list, every report and every export. A new surface that could show a salary must apply it before it ships.
The configuration is read at each request, so a change takes effect at once rather than at the next sign-in.
The configuration and its change history are retained 7 years, since they explain who could see what and when.

openQuestions.question: This rule says the School Admin cannot see any salary, while the salary use case makes the School Admin the one who sets it. The two cannot both hold, and the document says so explicitly. Either the School Admin is given sight of the salary section, or setting a salary moves to a role that can already see it.
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved. Nothing in this module can be built correctly until it is decided.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
